"Like The Wind" is a badly designed challenge. Using the ropes and other things along the course actually slows you down instead of speeding you up. A zombie simply breathing too close to you snaps you out of sprint. Even with near perfect runs I still am one second short of Gold.
Normally I wouldn't mind really difficult challenges and optional content in a game, but this particular challenge is part of a side quest. This is poor game design.

The game is great-ish. The story is meh. The faction mechanic is stupid.
If you like parkour and fighting zombies the game offers tens of hours of fun,
but if you're like me and want to complete all the quests then the DLC quest "The Master" will ruin your fun as it asks you to score Gold in three different challenges.
I am no longer young, my reflexes are slow, and I don't have the time, energy, nor inclination to get really good at any given game. I also refuse to cheat. And having a quest in my journal that I cannot complete will just annoy me and prevent me from enjoying the rest of the game. 
As such I am giving up on Dying Light 2. Uninstalled.

review.review:
I will recommend this game to anyone that has played Dying Light 1 or likes Open world RPGS. I spent 3 years slowly playing through this game with my best friend and had some of the best nights screaming like hell running from volatiles like they could get me through the screen. I have spend hours giggling at dumb glitches or watching my friend eat ♥♥♥♥ failing at a jump. Ending this game finally I'm left feeling lost and honestly grieving that the game has come to an end so soon, when it felt like it never would. 


Story: I did really enjoy this story line. And i LOVE Aiden and Jonah Scott did an OUTSTANDING job. But sometimes it felt like he was doing the heavy lifting during certain story beat moments. Some bigger side characters get sidelined and completely disappear sometimes depending on certain choices made. And it leaves you feeling a little confused and frustrated at times. Sometimes you just NEVER find big important things without googling. Writing this review I have a little over 100 hours and finished the game at level 8 and didn't even know about Jai I was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about not having anything other than a pistol this whole time? Another problem have is with how short this storyline is if you are not playing with the DLC or doing lots of side quests. You can enter the end game point at only level 5. I had assumed that the story would end at around level 8-9. So I was level 8 at the the boss fight and it made it SUPER easy unfortunately. I think the game really wants you to play both sides of peace keepers and survivors for more story beats but it really railroads you into choosing one. My last problem is with the important story choice moments. They give you about 30-25 seconds to choice between two options, Which I am not a big fan of but my bigger problem is after you choose it kind of just tells you what would happen if one choice is made, then it lets you choose AGAIN for real this time with no time limit. It gets rid of all sense of urgency and makes your choice not really feel in the moment.

Changes: During this games life span a lot of changes has happened to this game. One of them being getting rid of parkour using stamina. As much as this made my game play a little easier I felt like is lost something when they did that. Things became much easier and I felt it was a core important mechanic to keep. I felt that they should have just made moves cost slightly less stamina.

Bugs: As much as I love and enjoyed this game. It is super buggy playing co-op. If you aren't the one hosting the server and use an elevator once the doors open you WILL fall through the floor and be stuck downed in the elevator shaft. Sometimes I would open a door but it would remain stuck on the other persons end with them now trapped.  Sometimes zombies will just glitch and get you in a UV lit area. For how long this game has been out all of these problems really such have been fixed years ago.

Pros: Alot of fun with friends
Fun combat
Fun parkour
better crafting system
better weapon crafting and upgrading
lots of game play side quests and more
fun special events with special awards


Cons: SUPER buggy co-op and solo
most of your choices dont matter
main story line is SUPER short only need to be level 5 to start the end game
paraglider
controls on keyboard are a little iffy I would probably just commit to a controller if you can

Going into Dying Light, the game turned out to be much better than I expected.

The highlight is definitely the movement. Traversing the city using fluid parkour mechanics is fun, and racing to reach air drops across rooftops before anyone else is a great gameplay loop. The campaign also delivers a few impressive moments. The missions featuring Volatiles—the terrifying nocturnal creatures that are really hard to kill—bring genuine tension. Equally memorable is the mission where you climb to the very highest point in the city, which offers a great sense of scale.

The main drawback is the tedious scavenging. Constantly stopping to check endless crates, trash bins, and shelves for materials gets repetitive and slows down the pace.

Overall, Dying Light is a good game that holds up well thanks to its movement system and a few standout missions, even if the looting gets a bit repetitive.

game_name: Dying Light 2 Stay Human: Reloaded Edition

review.review:
190 hours in, and I'm still not done with it.

Dying Light 2 is one of those games that just keeps giving you reasons to stay. The parkour is the real star here — running, flying, and grappling across Villedor never stops feeling good, even hundreds of hours in. Combat has real weight to it, weapons degrade and break like the first DL (even if they dont show it), and the day/night cycle turning the city into a horror show once the sun goes down still gets my heart racing even after all this time.

The main story has its ups and downs — some genuinely great character moments mixed with pacing that drags in places — but the world itself carries the game. There's always another rooftop to climb, another GRE facility to loot, another Infected horde to either fight or flee from. Side quests are pretty good, but not all of them hit the same.

I also put a good chunk of hours into co-op, and it's a mixed bag — dropping into a friend's world and tackling hordes together is a blast and the parkour syncs up surprisingly well, but I ran into my share of bugs and sync issues (enemies desyncing, progress hiccups, the usual). Worth doing with people you're patient with.

About the DLCs, I played through both Bloody Ties and the content added in the Reloaded Edition. Bloody Ties is a fun, self-contained arena-style detour with its own flavor, while the Reloaded content adds some solid extra reasons to keep coming back if you've already cleared the main story or most other activities. 

Oh yeah right, the Agents system and Tower Raid mode. Uuhhhhhhhhhh, they're... something. If you want to spend 30 hours getting some cool weapons/skins, go ahead (only if you want 🙃). About Tower raid: try it once and see if you'll like; if yes, good for you, you will get bored eventualy anyway thoug; if not, congrats, you saved your hard-earned time :). Shame that the really interesting stuff is gatekeeped behind them but hey, what can we do about it.

So, the good:

Parkour and traversal are genuinely addictive
Combat is punchy and weapon variety keeps things fresh
Night gameplay is very tense (although not quite as DL1)
Huge amount of content — easily 60/100+ hours if you like exploring
Co-op adds a really fun extra layer (when it's working right)

The not-so-good:

Story pacing is uneven, some questionable writing choices
Co-op sync issues and bugs pop up more than I'd like
Some (if not all) side content feels repetitive by the late game
Good thing DLCs are basically free/implemented in the base game nowadays

If you liked the first game, or just want a huge, atmospheric open world built around movement, survival, and NOW some solid DLC content, this one's worth the time investment. Try also playing it with mods and the community maps are decent for passing the time. Recommended.

Backpedaling lore based reasons not to have firearms years after release was weird, but whatever, it was good incentive to come back and see what was new. The change that bothered me enough to finally write a review, and a negative one at that, was the cutting of the prologue. I can't imagine why anyone thought it was a good idea to cut important exposition and a beautiful look at the world we hadn't gotten before just to "speed players along to co-op and the open world". Especially when there was already a way to skip that part of the prologue! I'm so disappointed it's gone I don't really want to pick the game back up anymore. Whether or not anyone else feels that strongly is irrelevant, it's a symptom of a bigger problem. As much as I approve of maintaining older games, cutting content 4 years after release is ♥♥♥♥♥♥, and I'm concerned about what other changes Techland has planned for this game I love.

review.review:
Played the game expecting a sequel to the first one. Instead they reinvented the locations, the characters and the entire story in some weird way to try to adapt the story to the game and not the other way around.
In some ways I feel like the story was put together in a rush - as well as the entire game. Some events in the story feel completely unrealistic and somewhat chopped giving the idea that the original story was changed over and over again and when they couldn't change it in a way that would give it continuity, they add a seizure, a random enemy encounter that will knock you off or some completely unexpected thing just to make you spawn somewhere else and add a bit more to the tale.
This feeling of things put together also reflects in the build of some levels which are not clear sometimes on what the objectives are, what paths to take and given that this is a game with a lot of parkour, people will tend to explore various paths that might take you out of the mission area, feel completely bugged or just make you lose your time entirely thinking you are on the right path when you are just jumping to random placed ledge or object.
The lighting also feels too dark in a lot of areas, especially in story cutscenes where you should be able to easily understand what is happening without having to manually turn on the flashlight (and this is when you can).
There are also a lot of bugs especially in items you're able to search or interact with throught the game. Some of them are really worrying like backpacks you can only search when you're in a specific position, car trunks that you need to 'glitch' in order to open (and you can clip into the cars), interactible items cliping inside walls, tables, cars, etc...

TL;DR: The game is great, the story is good and has a lot of different endings (although I only played one), the parkour feels awesome when you master it and fighting zombies is just as good as the first game, although there are quite a number of bugs especially in story missions and the cutscenes lighting is really poor. 8/10 would recommend.

After playing Dying Light 2: Stay Human for the third time, I can honestly say that this playthrough felt completely different. With all the new recent updates I noticed that the story and the whole game is  completely improved. I liked that.

In this part of the franchise , we don't play as our beloved Kyle Crane, but as Aiden Caldwell —a boy who was experimented on as a child and is now searching for his only remaining family, his sister Mia. His journey is filled with mystery, pain, and difficult choices, making his story surprisingly emotional and engaging.

Dying Light 2 offers an amazing open world filled with activities, locations to explore, and plenty of things to discover. The story is gripping, and your choices can change the future of the characters and the world around you. Combined with well-written characters and an incredibly addictive combat system, there's always something pushing you forward.

The soundtracks are completely amazing!They add so much depth and emotion to Aiden's journey and the whole game itself.

The main story takes around 18–20 hours to complete, but if you're aiming for 100% completion, be prepared to spend a lot more time in the world. There's an enormous amount of content to explore and activities to complete.

Also I want to give special credit to Jonah Scott, Aiden's voice actor. His performance adds so much emotion and personality to Aiden, making him feel genuinely alive throughout the entire journey.

Overall, Dying Light 2: Stay Human is a new and refreshing chapter in the Dying Light universe. It may tell a different story with a different protagonist, but it still delivers the atmosphere, exploration, choices, and brutal combat that make Dying Light so enjoyable.

Though its verticality and new parkour tools make for fleeting moments of real evolution, Dying Light 2 is largely devoid of the soul and detail-oriented design that went into making the original installment such a timelessly excellent romp.

Zombies themselves lack the organic physics and environmental interactions that made them consistently compelling before, and gameplay on the whole is a rigid, over-baked impression of the fine-tuned movement mechanics we were previously spoiled with.

Though my memory is scarce at this point, what I could argue is that Dying Light 2 offers a more substantial endgame experience beyond the misery of the first game's Turtle grind, yet it ultimately serves no point when the endgame you're progressing is in service to mechanics and world design far inadequate to the pedigree its forefather established.

Easily an all-time disappointment on a level close to BioShock Infinite- though still certainly a far more consistently enjoyable experience than that schlock.

review.review:
They made a masterpiece with the original Dying Light, then said "alright let's just throw all that in the trash and make it worse in every way." I'm serious. The writing is so dreadful and the voice acting so laughable that I find myself skipping absolutely everything. Everything is either "haha funny fart poop marvel joke" or the most insufferable character ever which for some reason you decide to help because the writers deemed it appropriate.

The gameplay itself is just numbers-based and there's hardly any skill involved due to the braindead game design. There's an enemy that starts ringing an alarm to summon others, but the windup takes a few seconds, but the thing is it absolutely doesn't matter if you kill him before he finishes it since the enemies will come anyways. Why? Because the game designer said so.

Fast enemies called virals are supposed to be attracted to noise, but will start spawning around you (crawling under cars, out of holes in buildings, or literally OUT OF THE PAVEMENT) even if you just fight anyone with standard melee weapons. Why? Because the game designer said so.

There's a stealth mechanic where you can stealth kill enemies, but somehow the game just says "lol no" without any indication and just makes them survive, whereupon they alert all other enemies in the zone. Why? Because the game designer said so.

You can be in a night chase and outrun your enemies, but more will start spawning COMPLETELY RANDOMLY in front of you. Why? Because the game designer said so.

Speaking of nighttime, let's talk about what was probably the most idiotic decision in the history of game design - giving you a FIVE MINUTE TIMER that kills you when it runs out whenever you're out of sunlight or UV light. The infected are already more numerous and faster at night, and Volatiles (which are practically unkillable on the highest difficulty and will two-shot you) spawn, so there is already enough risk at night to counterbalance the reward, not to mention that most of the areas you want to go to are only accessible at night. This means that if you like the extra risk of playing mostly at night, you'll find yourself constantly darting between safe houses to refill your immunity bar, because the items that restore it are few and far between and require the same resources as first aid kits to produce, which is very rare if you don't purposefully farm it (why the hell would you want to farm in an action game that's supposed to be about parkour and speed).

All enemies have phantom range, hitting you when you're clearly away from them. I've been hit by horizontal swings from enemies when I'm on platforms above their heads, and stabbed by knives that were nowhere close to me. Whenever an attack comes you have to dodge, because using spacing will punish you every time.

And the bugs... I cannot believe how buggy this game is over 4 years after release. Your weapon which you've invested everything in will vanish randomly. Enemies will glitch out and freeze still, becoming invulnerable. Your character will decide he doesn't want to grab ledges and fall to his death. You will kill enemies which are basically loot goblins, but they will bug out and become unlootable. Encounter rewards won't be given because the NPC will freeze. There's a bug every few minutes and it'll keep you in a constant state of annoyance.

Overall it's all just very tiresome. Play the first one if you haven't already, or replay it if you have. I might just rush to finish this one ASAP since I'm playing with someone else, but if you can stay away.

But man, some of the side characters are terrible. Barney, Sophie, and Lawan are what really brought this game down to the dump. Hakon, who's the only cool side character, turns out to be a traitor is just poor writing by definition. I don't wanna compare, but Dying Light 1's characters were special compared to Dying Light 2's. Brecken, Jade, Rahim, Karim, and Amir (who has 10 seconds of screen time is still a better character than some in Dying Light 2) are all characters you love and don't want to see gone. The mechanics in this game I'm mixed about The forsaken stores, dark hallows, and gre anomalies are pretty cool and don't leave your experience dry. I gave it a thumbs-up for lack of a middle-of-the-road button. Frankly, it'd seem silly to show I've put in 100+ hours and not recommend it. 

Forgive the politics, but it feels like a game of the times, made with neoliberal values. They probably did a stack of research and focus group discussions to figure out how to keep players in the game for as long as possible, and they somehow managed to do that without making it particularly good. The search for those often hard-to-reach inhibitors, the next parkour or combat level, or valuable crafting components keep you exploring, doing the side quests, fighting through infested research facilities. Unfortunately, this process feels more like grinding than perhaps it could, as the game is hampered by paper-thin characters, annoyingly inane side quests, and mediocre writing and voice acting. Things that, when done well, sadly aren't guranteed to make a game a commercial success. It was great to 'see' Rosario Dawson in a key role, but even she seemed to struggle to deal with the verbal clunk. 

There are still plenty of glitches. I've walked through surfaces, been respawned in a room with no exit and have often been unable to pick up enemy loot left over in place of bodies.

There are redeeming things that were evidently enough to keep me playing. The weapon and item upgrade system is OK, the parkour's good, and it's an interesting environment to explore - even if its repetitiveness makes itself apparent fairly early. The day-night cycle - and the heightened sense of danger at night - remain among the game's biggest strengths, even if they've been de-emphasised a bit.

Do I recommend it? I don't know, I guess so. If you're a fan of the first game, you should get something (if a little less) out of this entry in the series. But I don't recommend the Bloody Ties DLC - not much to offer there aside from boring grinding.

review.review:
I really wanted to like this game due to my fascination of DL1. It falls short of the "enjoyment" factor that I found and liked in the previous game. Don't get me wrong DL2 is a very good game! Gameplay, graphics, world and environment - it improves on everything and then some.
On a serious thought, it feels like a mixed-bag for me. So let me try and pin down what I like vs what I disliked.
Liked -
1. Guns (better late than never)
2. Parkour (order of magnitude better)
3. Graphics (so much details in the world)
4. Story (it is a good story that could have done better)
5. Weapons (appreciate the included weapons and the mod system. Really like the variety in thrown knives)
6. Extra activities (a bunch of side-quests that keep you engaged. Some are too good)
7. Co-op (DL games are best played with a friend)
8. Community (integrates community created maps download, and modding options like TPP without leaving the game!)

Disliked -
1. Guns (still limited variety in story. Feels ornamental when using in tower raid without upgrades)
2. Parkour (grappling hook is now crippled and more realistic?)
3. Graphics (options missing. does not run smoothly at native resolution on my 3070 mobile)
4. Story (it could have just as well have been a good side story. you can feel it lacking to be a main story)
5. Weapons (its a melee favored game just like the first DL. Guns seem to be an afterthought and feel un-balanced at times)
6. Extra activities (some of them are better than the main story and that makes me sad)
7. Co-op (disconnects some times and gives you a generic reason. like trying to join during a cutscene)
8. Community (you have to log in to use these benefits. understandable, but also could have done without it in some cases)
9. DLCs and Add-ons (the first expansion is also its last. want better guns? get DL points with real money and then proceed to buy it in-game. short on some? get another one. totally optional)
10. Editions (no Ultimate Edition with everything included, yet. There was one but they cancelled it before launching DL Beast. They promised something they could not follow through due to the said game upgrading from DLC status to a fully standalone experience)
11. Updates (I like it that it still receives updates, but seeing how the game still has a lot of issues is really annoying. Also its slow to update compared to other titles I have played on Steam. Something to do with patches)

review.review: One of the best games I've ever played. I've just finished the story as of writing this and will do my utmost to avoid any spoilers. But, wow. When I say this game is incredible, I mean it. Techland may be a controversial bunch according to others, but man, they've crafted one hell of a game with Dying Light 2. Everything from combat, parkour, story, and activities, are so well made. I've played only a small amount of Dying Light 1 to actually make a valid comparison, but that doesn't stop me from saying this: If you loved the first Dying Light and or are looking to pick up an absolute gem of a zombie game, this is the game for you. The game's setting takes place in the last city standing 15 years after the collapse of humanity, and man does it do a great job at portraying that. Running across lush green rooftops reclaimed by nature never gets old and is always viable throughout the entire game. I love games that feature skill trees and make you feel like you're actually progressing through the game, and boy let me tell you this game does an excellent job at it. Gaining skills and using those skills to the player's benefit never gets old. There is also a multitude of tools and gadgets for the player to use, from a UV light that repels zombies, to a literal paraglider that allows for easy traversal of the game's map. Did I neglect to mention the map? Well its about twice the size of the first game's map and focuses more on verticality (especially in the Central Loop). The first "act" of the game takes place in the lesser part of the main city Villedor. This part is generally considered an early game area, with rooftops being much more easy to get to than later on. But, as the story progresses, you eventually get access to the Central loop. This is considered the biggest part of the game not only in width, but in verticality. This is where the game tests all of the skills and tactics learned by the player in old villedor, and puts them to the test. Running along rooftops and climbing to them isn't a light task anymore, it's a challenge each time. But what I cannot put enough emphasis on is the beauty of these areas. Everywhere you go you experience lush green nature reclaimed buildings and vines that seem to almost never end. I love the idea of humanity's greatest structures being mashed together with beautiful green flora. Enough blabber about the setting, lets dive into gameplay. Boy oh boy where do I start. I played the game through with normal difficulty and physical parkour. Everything is responsive and works together. The parkour is dynamic and the map feels as if it was built for parkour, which is rare in a lot of games today. The combat feels heavy and responsive with meaty swings and abysmal levels of gore. From slicing people and zombies in half, to full on decapitating them, the combat flow never gets old and only improves as more skills are unlocked. The story is actually really interesting and absolutely had some parts that made me tear up (I'm a whole ass dude btw). The narrative was easy to follow along and left room to wonder and curiosity as I kept playing. The voice acting is incredible, every conversation felt real and not like I was talking to a person reading a script. The civil war style of factions in the city feels incredible and lets the player decide who to side with. The graphics are incredible with shockingly amazing performance. I played this game on a laptop with 12gb of ram and still managed to easily capture a steady 90-120 fps. All in all, this game was so worth it. I enjoyed every second of this game I played. 10/10.

The main reason I'm even playing this game is to understand the lore before jumping into Dying Light: The Beast, but aside from that, this game doesn't really compare to the original.

First off, the story is pretty underwhelming. Stuff just kind of happens with little to no build-up, so even when something "big" occurs, it doesn't land or feel interesting. Being more "realistic" doesn't automatically make it better than the first game.

The combat is rough — you'll dodge an attack clean, and then the enemy randomly teleports a few centimeters forward and still hits you. Parkour also feels way slower and clunkier; getting to the top of one taller building can mean routing around four other buildings just to find a path up.

Overall, not worth 60 euros at launch price. Wait for a sale if you're interested

Techland did NOT learn from the first game.

The writing somehow dropped quality, and that's saying something as the first game had absolute terrible writing.
The dialogue is so bad, you can't help but laugh at it. Both the performance of most VAs and the actually writing is really bad. Game logic doesn't exist, people and things fade in and out of the scenes depending on when the game script calls for it. People literally teleport across the map for specific cutscenes.

The story is abysmal and non-sensical. The amount of cutscenes has jumped 1,000,000 in the first game to 6,000,000 in this one. Cutscenes for literally nothing, ones of opening doors, just to walk 5ft for another cutscene to play of you walking down a hallway. Clunky animations and awkward transitions make the game's "most serious moments" as the funniest scenes in gaming. 

The characters are all 1 dimensional archetypes. You have the leader archetype, the badass archetype, the misunderstood archetype. They never deviate from their set archetype.

The combat is actually somehow worse and more annoying in this one. Completely turned into slapping the enemy until it dies. Complete tank-y enemies.

The HUD and UI is terrible. A poorly done Far Cry 6 style UI, and that's saying something. Constant pop-ups that you have to hold space for 5 seconds to close, telling you such vital information like "how to crouch". Amazing.

Performance is also terrible. Never have I played a game that looks terrible and lags to ♥♥♥♥ at the same time, on both highest and lowest graphics settings. 

The parkour feels so much WORSE than the first game, way more floaty and on railed. The map design doesn't help it since it feels like the map belongs in a different game and not made for the parkour system. The verticality of the map is supposed to enhance the system but it just makes it more tedious and annoying. 

This game is actually terrible and I will never play it again. Never make another game Techland. Please.

100 hours and 1 save file.
This is one of the most fun, satisfying and violent games i have ever had the pleasure of playing. Jumping from lamp post to rooftop, wall running across a billboard and drop kicking a zombie having a mid-day snack before proceeding to delete it's face with the soles of my fresh kicks. 10/10 no notes.

What i do have notes for however, is the story. I don't know if my way of playing was the problem or if it just didn't make sense altogether, because I'd be having the time of my life for a couple play sessions straight just parkouring, decimating dead people, and levelling up and unlocking more ways to parkour and decimate dead people. So by the time I'd decide to do some story missions, id be pretty lost..
Characters i never remembered came and went, some in forced 'emotional' moments which just had me thinking...okay.... And the few characters which did leave an impression on me kinda just disappeared????
It's clear that the gameplay is the main show here and boy does the game excel at that, but the story is too hard to ignore especially since a lot of gameplay mechanics are locked behind it. I didn't unlock guns until 92 hours in because they were locked behind an unsuspecting side quest.
And when i arrived at the grand finale, I FUMBLED IT SOOOO HARD. You have to make a lot of choices throughout the story and when it's time to pick one (imo) they're kinda vague/unclear. At the final decision, i was given 2 options, one i understood and one i thought i understood. I picked the second option. I should not have picked the second option.  In a game where there's a lot of (monotonous) dialogue, there is no way to see the important stuff when you need it most. in my case, leading to a nuclear level event. oopsie ig. 

This game is best when you boot it up for a few hours to pull off some insane parkour moves and fight waves of undead, preferably with some sick music on to fuel your exploits. Dying Light 2 + Bring Me The Horizon = must try. no pressure tho.
It goes on sale a couple times a year for about £20. i strongly recommend giving it a go, just don't take it too seriously :))

review.review:
Positive part of the game:
1) The parkour system has become more interesting;
2) A relatively improved combat system - fights with NPCs are now more varied, but at the same time, spamming a single move like a dropkick lets you gain the upper hand against all enemies except those who are not affected by this, although all of them can easily die by maxed-out throwing knives;
3) OST is overall good;
4) Old Villedor does a good job of capturing the feel of the old town from the first game; it’s even fun to do side quests there;
5) An OK atmosphere.

Now, moving to the
Negative part of the game:

1) Terrible controls, because the developers chose to prioritize console gameplay and made the controls firstly for gamepads, thus every skill is activated by its own button. Comparing to the first DL, buttons had multiple actions bounded to them, but here they didn't even think to assign aiming with ranged weapons to the same button used for blocking. Option to assign multiple actions to one button is also not included, so the only proper way out of it was to download a mod that changed controls to be for like from the first DL.

2) Because the game prioritizes controller play, the player often has to hold down the interaction button. For me personally, this is extremely annoying, because it wasn’t like that in the first game, and the gameplay felt more dynamic than standing still and staring at a single spot for several seconds just to trigger an action.

3) Censorship. Game still has a lot of hanged bodies and you can sever limbs as well as smash people's head and watch brains spill out, but a cutscene with hanging has been replaced with a black screen.

4) Annoying merchants with their irritating comments when you're buying/selling. Every transaction is accompanied by a pointless, repetitive line delivered in an irritating tone.

5) Jai deserves a point separate from 4th. You get the distinct feeling that the developers were full of shіt while coming up with the idea that, to buy items from him, you're strongly encouraged, or better to say almost forced to play in co-op. The quests he gives are mindless grinding, since you’ll have to replay missions 20 times and hope you’ll have enough points to buy something new, rather than to just get ammo resupply for your pistol (and i don't want to waste time to farm 20–30 rounds from convoys or hunt armored infected, if you’re lucky). After unlocking a shotgun, i instantly lost interest in all those quests without any desire to get any other weapon from him.

6) Explanations for certain new features. The entire game pauses and starts explaining to you what, where, and how things work with this or that new mechanic, etc. The immersion drops below zero.

7) Despite writing a positive comment about combat, NPC still are not interesting to fight due to the reasons aforementioned there. It seems that nobody but player can use grenades, makeshift guns and other stuff, and it looks like AI doesn't have any tactics at all to make a fight more engaging and interesting.

8) The game does absolutely everything it can to make the player spend a ton of time playing. The city feels both enormous and empty at the same time. Aside from the paraglider and the grappling hook (which unlocks too late and I never used it anywhere except for story missions), there’s no transportation, but there's fast travel, which you still have to unlock and which only becomes available after completing a significant portion of the main story. This also includes the lack of an adequate save system in the game, where your choices determine future events and character development. The game allows you to rewind your progress, but you can only rewind to the moment when you've completed your last main quest. In other words, if you’ve been doing side quests for several hours and would like to replay one of them with different choices - you have to rewind several hours back to the point when you finished the main quest and redo absolutely everything. Not even mentioning stuff like Chapter Agents and so on, but I get a feeling that they were added also just to make players waste even more time on the game.

Jumping to the conclusion, I am genuinely disappointed in this game, as it looks like it's worse in almost everything than its predecessor. It's worth only to accomplish the main story once, or twice if you're that stubborn. Personally, I'd get more satisfaction from replaying first DL with its story DLC on Nightmare difficulty and doing quests there, than replaying this game.

This game is sickeningly long. I felt like I was doing side quest after side quest the entire MAIN STORYLINE. Half of the decisions made by the people who will "help you" find  your sister don't end up getting fulfilled and any that do follow up on their promise to Aiden do it in such a poorly attempted manner it's genuinely laughable. It pains me to hate on this game so heavily, but Dying Light 1 has been played for almost 1000 hrs for me on PC alone and this second one just ain't it. Parkour IS better in my opinion but animations are so buggy most improvements are immediantely out of the picture. I also lose momentum randomly just because. The sheer amount of bugs in this game are horrible as well. I really WANT to like this game, but I just can't. Save your money or just buy the first one. I'm gonna open google docs and finish this review in a script for a video someday. The world needs to know how awful this game is.

Horribly optimized. Why are the enemies still loading mid cutscene, after I killed them (they were invisible and I bumped into them accidentally) why is Aiden grunted 10 minutes after I swung my machete, why are cutscenes muted and I have to rely on subtitles to get the "full experience"? Why are all textures missing and replaced with gray blobs? This is while the game takes its sweet time loading EVERY time I open it mind you. My graphics card is a 4070 Geforce NTX so it can definitely handle it...pretty sure GTA loads faster than the entirety of this game does.  
Why in the world does the game take so long to open with the intro cutscene set to off? I would be loading in faster with the whole thing playing before my gameplay at this point. WHY do multiple voice lines play simultaneously numerous times throughout the story? WHY IN THE WORLD does the music cut in and out and get replaced with some annoying wind blowing sound effect. This game has been out for 4 years and yes Techland has patched numerous day one bugs but seriously, why are we not prioritizing optimization issues first? Consoles that can run at a max of 60 fps do better with this game than my $2000 gaming pc for goodness sakes. Forget about turning on a fun game after work, this bad boy will take you at least 20 minutes to start feeling playable. 

The game itself is fun. I just wish I could enjoy it without constantly wondering if I could fix a visual bug by changing my settings and I wish I could've enjoyed it DURING the main storyline as well.

review.review:
This negative review isn't about the quality of Dying Light 2 but about the removal of the prologue and other early content. On the contrary, I'm playing all 3 Dying Lights simultaneously and 2 is currently my favorite, minus the combat.

When I heard they had cut so much from the beginning, I had to see it for myself. So I played through an older version of the game first. After falling in love with it, I got the game here for full price.

Their removal of the prologue truly butchered the emotional weight of the setting and the inner turmoil of the protagonist with regards to both his personal quest and the choices he makes as a foreigner of Villedor. It's a damn shame how much it compromises and skews the original story. The original intro to this game and its characters was so good! It's what got me hooked in the first place.

I don't understand what this decision was even for. There was already a "skip prologue" option for people who don't care about the story and want to jump straight into the action. If my first experience had been the abridged game through Steam, I'm sad to say I probably would have refunded it.

After further playtime, I'm realizing too that they completely removed stamina drain from the parkour. While it was certainly more friction than the free climbing of DL1, it was a mechanic that differentiated DL2 from the rest and made climbing more like a puzzle at times. There's not even a toggle to re-enable the stamina drain.

I really hope they reconsider their decision and add back in all the content they removed. It feels like the game lost its soul.

EDIT: After finishing the campaign, here's my actual review of the game itself. Though my recommendation of buying the game here won't change to positive until cut content has been restored.

Incredibly fun game blending parkour with good old zombie smashing. Play it for the gameplay, not the plot.

The story starts off strong but admittedly loses steam and focus as it goes on. The characters are nuanced and interesting until they make baffling, illogical decisions. The voice acting is really well done until multiple characters pronounce the same person's name differently. The story beats are engaging until the ending completely ruins everything. Overall the campaign side of things is serviceable but very flawed.

The mechanics are where Dying Light has always shined. Parkour moves are varied and engaging. Very little is done automatically for you so there's a lot of autonomy in your traversal of the city. The paraglider is a lot of fun for airborne traversal. Combat is visceral and weighty. Enemies respond to repetitive attacks to encourage you to keep your approaches varied. Looting materials and crafting mods to electrify, ignite, envenom, etc. your weapons is fulfilling. It's the sort of game where you can run around simply enjoying the feeling of the game at its core--a zombie parkour sandbox.

[h1]My Rating: 4/5[/h1]

[h3] Dying Light 2 [/h3]

As much as I love Dying Light 1, I cannot recommend  Dying Light 2. This game in its current state. There are simply too many bugs, the game crashes far too often, and the gameplay itself can feel extremely repetitive.

[b] The Good [/b]

There are definitely some things I really like about the game. Some of the side quests are genuinely unique and wonderfully written. The story is also good, and I really like the idea of having choices that can have an impact on the game. The atmosphere and the overall concept of Dying Light 2 are great.

[b] Bugs and Crashes [/b]

Unfortunately, the biggest problem for me is the stability of the game. It crashed so many times that I lost [u] 30+ hours of progress [/u] and had to repeat parts of the game several times. 

I also play on the [u] lowest graphical settings [/u] , yet I still experience frequent FPS drops. Considering the low settings I'm using, this is especially disappointing.

[b] Achievements [/b]

The achievement system is another major issue.

Some achievements are straight-up frustrating or poorly designed. There was one achievement I couldn't get without using a controller, while another one simply refused to update properly.

There are also situations where you can apparently unlock an achievement too early, even though you haven't actually reached the point where you should be able to get it.

Another frustrating aspect is that some collectibles can be missed depending on your choices. This can be extremely annoying if you're trying to complete the game.

[b] Overall [/b]

I really want to like Dying Light 2, because there is a lot of potential here. The story is good, some of the side quests are excellent, and the idea of choices affecting the game is great.

However, the frequent crashes, lost progress, FPS drops, repetitive gameplay, and frustrating achievement system make it very difficult for me to recommend.

I love the Dying Light franchise, but unfortunately, I cannot recommend it because of its technical issues and frustrating design choices.

review.review:
Techland made a parkour zombie game so focused on movement that it accidentally became a masterpiece at making you feel like you're actually running for your life instead of just pressing buttons. The parkour system is genuinely excellent — fluid, responsive, and forgiving enough that you're chaining vaults and wall-runs without the controller input feeling like a rage-quit waiting to happen.

The Reloaded Edition is the "live service redemption" version: Techland shipped a messy launch in 2022 (bugs, bugs everywhere), then spent two years actually fixing it. The improvements landed, the arsenal expanded with guns, and 10+ post-launch updates smoothed the rough edges. Day/night cycles create genuine tension — daylight means you're looting and progressing, night means you're either parkour-sprinting or finding shelter because the zombies turn fast. That pacing works.

The story is weak (Aiden's characterization is paper-thin, your faction choices feel less consequential than advertised), and some quests can become unavailable through poor planning, which is annoying rather than clever. But the open world's verticality rewards exploration, co-op is functional, and the melee combat is satisfying enough to make zombie encounters feel like something other than QTE theater.

The technical issues that plagued launch are largely gone. The grind for certain achievements (960km of running? seriously?) is tedious, but 100% completion is achievable without wanting to unalive yourself.

It's a step down from the first game (fans universally agree DL1 is better), but as a standalone parkour-zombie experience at a steep discount, this is genuinely worth your time. Get it on sale, install it, and spend 80+ hours just moving through a dead city.

review.review:
TL:DR 
Mechanics are pretty decent, a lot more polished than the buggy mess that was the first games parkour and combat, and exploration is overall pretty fun if you're into that.
Butt (and it's a big Butt) the story, characters and mode of story telling are so bad it's not even funny, and do not be mistaken, the parkour and combat still feels quite wonky at times.
Certain quests and situations will bug out, I had several break on me where I had to find alternative solutions or look up bug fixes online.

Though, if you like endlessly grinding in an open world, slaughtering zombies by the dozen and slowly looting them, this could easily be for you. (If you are easily annoyed by bad story, characters, forcing modern ideology into stories etc, I'd read the full review though).

At first I though I'd be recommending it, the afformention Big Butt is why I don't.

Now onto the review.

[h2]The Good:[/h2]

[h3] Mechanics [/h3]
As mentioned above, combat and parkour are vastly improved from the first game.
Your weapons feel more kill-y, there's more gore, there's less "enemies get priority moves" like in the first game, and when you've unlocked a bunch of moves, parkour starts to feel quite fast and fluid, though it does take a bit for it to start feeling really good, and there's the caveat that as you gain more moves, the system starts to break a little more, or become more unwieldy in certain situations.

[h3]The Exploration [/h3]
Feels good, lots to see, lots to do, if you're the kind that likes random quests and encounters that feel... Somewhat varied but still repeating ofc, since it is a game, this could be for you.
Grapling hook is very nieché in this game, where it felt amazing in the first game. (But it's great for breaking the [spoiler] "turning" [/spoiler] animations if you just wanna get on with it, this is the good part).
[spoiler] Paraglider [/spoiler] It's pretty fun, good addition to the arsenal, needs to be fully upgraded before becoming powerful enough to be really fun though.

- Might be really fun in Co-op. haven't had the chance to test that, but honestly not sure (Doesn't seem like it to me, maybe if you can go into the Tower Roguelite mode together).

[h2]The Bad:[/h2]

[h3] Story [/h3]
Oh boy the story.
The twists they make in the storytelling are something a 12 year old with basic media literacy can figure out several hours in advance.
Few of the character are noteworthy, and some they try [b] So Hard [/b] to make you care about.
In one case even forcing A MAIN STORY QUEST to literally just be a humiliation ritual/emotional whatever moment with one of the characters (one that I absolutely disliked from the first time I met them and therefore, if there was any player agency/choice, I would have just left).
The promised speech system and choices are very limited, basically only being able to make major choices and even those feel... Underwhelming, at time.
Plus tons of DEI, absolute metric ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of it.

[h3] Continuity & More [/h3]
Several times I could've sworn I was told certain characters had died, or specific situations had happened etc.
Then the character turns up alive somehow, or when I went back to check the area of said MAJOR story event, literally no living soul is left, or no sign of said event ever occuring.

[h2]The Ugly:[/h2]

[h3]The Mode of Storytelling[/h3]
Its awful, so many times you're entering the presence of major character and what not, and the game just takes over and does things for you (even though it was portrayed as having choices and roleplaying). 
These moments are even worse when it's, as a simple example, you sneaking into an enemy base, only for the cutscenes to decide that you get jumped from behind and taken prisoner, despite me as the player (before it even happens on screen) thinking "Ok so we're about to get jumped, maybe turn around for just a micro second to not get bonked on the noggin?".
Plus several scenes that (I haven't confirmed, not sure I cba to confirm) feel as if they are meant to happen, and even if you get a choice, nothing really changes.

[h3]The Characters.[/h3]
Major themes with these include; The most obvious betrayals ever, Not judging a book by its cover(Or the next book, or the next book, or the next...), The most obvious twist characters ever written, and ofc GirlBosses are always better than Men, whom are (as exemplified by most of the male characters in this game) useless drunkards, unreliable, bullheaded, stupid, or simply betray you, also whenever something bad happens only GirlBoss can save you, you useless pathetic Main Character whom has been hardened by a life on the road that to most seems almost impossible due to how difficult it is, and that just did a bunch of stuff everyone actually thought completely impossible, but no call GirlBoss immediately so she can save you! 
While the women (even GirlBosses) are demeaned to being overly emotional, easy to anger, easily spooked/panicked, prone to taking actions counter to anything logical/reasonable simply because, but still controlling and manipulative somehow (which is so easy to do to with those stupid horny men).
However most of the time still at least not betraying you outright like all the evil men do! (Aka Insufferable feminist ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥).

If you've played Dying Light 1, the gameplay for 2 is pretty bland. I don't get sucked into the story even remotely and there's no part of it that feels new. 

Honestly, I found myself wanting to cheer for the bad guys, because theres no faction politics that seems interesting and 0 dimensions and poor story arcs. A lot of the tasks felt tedious and gave almost no advancement or advantage. Then, they tried to make it seem like "oooooh you could betray these good guys for a quick trip to area 2... what a tough decision" and i'm all, "yes please!" because i was so bored with the 2 dimensional characters in area 1.

Im gonna come back and finish it *someday* but until then, its going to stay pretty deep in my Backlogs.
Sidenote: there were some minor political subthemes i did not find enjoyable, and others might not as well, but im not mad. They can write whatever they want to their games.

review.review:
10/10 would play again

-- Pros --

Really enjoyed my time with Dying Light 2 Reloaded Edition. The visuals are great, the world is immersive, and there's a ton of content packed into the story. The parkour also does a great job of keeping that classic Dying Light feeling alive.

That said, this game was 10x better with a friend. Co-op created a lot of unique moments, especially when it came to the choices. Being able to decide who to save, which side to support, and seeing how those choices played out made the story a lot more fun to experience together. Sometimes we agreed, sometimes we didn't, and that's part of what made it enjoyable.

Exploring the city, messing around with the parkour, fighting infected and just seeing what kind of trouble we could get into with two people made for some of my favorite moments.


-- Cons --

There are definitely some bugs though. We ran into a few visual glitches and some story interaction/progression issues while playing co-op. Nothing that ruined the game for us, but they were noticeable and sort of annoying. 

And then there's the Forbidden Elevator.

We had a power station where the power was ON, but the game absolutely refused to let us use the elevator or capture the location. We tried everything. I ended up fixing it by restarting the game and completing it solo. 

Overall, I think the pros outweighed the cons, it honestly was a really fun and rewarding experience.

review.review:
Remove the best parts of the first game, water it down, and you end up with Dying Light 2. DL1 you start weak and slowly get stronger but the game emphasized the fun parts of parkour and integrating that into a unique combat system. Also did a great job with the fear of getting mobbed or going out at night. UI was simple and it kept the bland parts of the game from getting in the way. Had some janky bits and wasn't perfect but was still a great game.
DL2, you spend most if not all of your time in the bland parts. Inventory management is awful and slow. Every quest is a fetch quest and I can't even begin to care about the characters involved. Tons of quests and challenges to do but all of them are just surface level garbage. The environment itself is boring. Wide open and less zombies which leads to long times of paragliding instead of running and gunning. Put it all together and it just doesn't even feel worth completing. Sad that it couldn't capture the magic that DL1 had. I gave it as long as I could before giving up, hoping that it would improve but ended up bored, annoyed, and disappointed.

review.review:
//HUGE SPOILERS//

My husband and I got this game together after beating the first one. Preface, we were disappointed with the first one's ending too. Then we played the DLC, which was mid. Transitioning into this second game, I consider it the most disappointing, and quite a let down in contrast to the first one in really every way. 

The characters were mostly unlikeable and very gaslighty for all your fetch quests which makes up the bulk of the game - I really dislike games where you're just getting stupid stuff done for useless people but then in cutscenes they're saving you somehow. Someone's always saying 'hurry up, aiden!' and doing literally nothing, and it's so redundant it became in inside joke. 

I didn't feel inclined to help the rebels, or the peace keepers, but ultimately chose the latter just out of curiosity. The game leans towards the rebels are the 'moral' option, but Sophie literally just sends her people to the slaughter and then blames everyone else -- there's even a part where she comically lists everyone thats died for her, while she sits safely on the inside yelling orders that gets people killed, while she's doing nothing. The peace keepers aren't that great either, but at least they were kinda interesting and not wrapped up in the 'my dead parents life goal is my whole personality, we're just angsty orphans' trope.

The character development for the majority of them is very poor, and both the npcs and aiden are extremely contradictive, to the point where aidens responses and decisions (beyond the few you can make, that hardly matter) are almost always out of character. In the fights that matter, hes usually losing, which makes no sense given the point you're at in the game level and weapon wise. 

Lawan was also an extremely annoying 'romantic interest' that you're just kinda stuck with the whole game - her quests are largely just stupid for an apocalyptic setting, like "go get my shoes im mad at you". You spend so much time flying around the map apologizing for every little thing that upsets her, while she tells you you're stupid but she loves you, and don't 'mother hen' her while she does that exact thing to you all the time. Oh and also, my favorite, "hurry up, aiden!" I keep thinking, is this a zombie game or a low quality romance simulator with some zombies in the background?? 

and where tf did jack go at the end like he just ran away from a missile and disappeared, I didn't get an option to hunt him down or kill him there. ppl just teeheeing away all the time like. 

the ending glitched out for me, so after mia dies i got end credits and then the screen went black and kicked me out of the game. :) from a buggy perspective, this game is SO buggy, in one session (with great internet connection and fairly powerful computers) we had to close the game and relaunch, over and over. Which sometimes was to our benefit, because we'd be able to skip an annoying part of a quest and be teleported to where we needed to be. Othertimes, you're losing loot because the zombies you killed are non interactive, your jumping all around the map unable to interact with anything, stuck on a random staircase, oh and my FAVORITE is when you're doing the incredibly unfun and redundant generator quests, and your coop member falls through the elevator and dies, meanwhile for the host is trying to get through the ever resetting elevator doors that keep opening and closing. When playing coop, the interface also gets confused if you play with someone further ahead than you, and marks areas as completed because they did it in their run through but you did not in yours. 

I cannot recommend this game, personally, because it felt like that movie theater moment where you go 'wait thats it? its over?" and if you're wondering -- "well gee spicy you couldnt hate it that much you have 68 hours" - most of that was spent reloading due to glitches, screaming at my monitor while i try to use the stupid paraglider to get to the top of another generic building, or doing one of the very few fun things in the game imo which is hunting down "backpack guys" while being chased by volatiles and trying to get good free weapons (because the bounties were kind of annoying as you can only track 2 at a time and have to keep running back to the same place, submitting, and then get 2 more). 

Would not play again, but if you have a friend that you want to get into silly situations with, this could be, at the least, entertaining for the 30 hours or so of gameplay that's really there. The zombie chase at night will always be fun, would be even more fun if they dropped better loot...

Played the game earlier and actually liked it. Parkour and zombies is just a great combo in my book. 
Just now (August 26) reinstalled and found out: the "refined" shortened prologue that came with the Reloaded update, removed big parts of the start of the game, completely cut a character that also served as a connection between the first game and this one, and skipped a lot of gameplay, world building and with it a lot of identity of the setting.
After reaching the city it's pretty much the same, but seriously, this is just cut content in the worst way possible. 
I'd love to give a positive review but nope. I don't want to speculate why it was actualle made, but it was a really bad decision in my book, and thus: No. Do not buy. Who know what, or whom, they cut next. 
Patch the prologue back in and I'll change this review.
